text:
jordan: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime patch we're seeing a KV prefix-cache hit-rate drop and p99 token latency increase. cc @anya @sam, any quick ideas?

perf-bot: CI perf alert: infra/main → perf_regression detected (link: https://ci.redwood/alerts/9842) :rotating_light:

anya: I ran a quick profile. Two things jump out: kernel selection is flipping to a slower fallback for short seqs when batches mix long+short, and our cache keying is too fragile (trailing spaces / minor tokenization diffs cause fragmentation).

sam: Telemetry snapshot (last 6h):
```
kv_cache_hit_rate: 62.3%  (baseline ~83%)
avg_tokens_per_gpu: -18%
p99_gen_latency: 320ms (was 210ms)
batch_size_dist: p50=3, p90=6, long_tail: 35% batches >4
```
Batch median size didn't move much but batch composition is much more heterogeneous.

jordan: So continuous batching may be the culprit — it groups by arrival time, not prefix. If a batch contains many different prefixes we lose KV reuse and also pick kernels based on avg_seq_len that aren't optimal for most requests.

miguel: Exactly. Continuous batching is great for throughput but it doesn't optimize for prefix locality. Two quick mitigations: (1) pre-warm top-K prefixes on deploy, (2) short hold-window (eg 3-5ms) to coalesce same-prefix arrivals. Both are low-effort to prototype.

anya: On keying: we should switch to a normalized prefix hash: `model_id + prefix_token_ids_normalized` (trim trailing whitespace tokens, collapse repeated spaces). That reduced fragmentation in staging a bit. Also add a small LRU for fragment-level caching (prefix fragments of length 16/32 tokens) to improve partial matches.

sam: We tried normalization in staging last week — +3pp hit-rate, not enough alone. The missing piece is batch homogeneity. If we can get batches with fewer distinct prefix_hash values we get multiplicative benefits.

miguel: There's also kernel selection interplay: runtime picks kernel based on batch average seq_len. If you group short + long all together, short requests pay the fallback cost. We can bias kernel choice by majority seq_len or prefer per-request microkernels if hardware supports.

anya: Profiler also shows lock contention in `kv_get` path when many misses trigger async loads. A per-shard optimistic fast-path (check without global lock) reduces stall time on misses. I can prototype that.

jordan: Quick tradeoffs: holding requests for 5ms increases tail latency for singletons but could increase overall hit-rate and reduce p99 later. Need to quantify.

sam: I'll run queueing sims and a microbench: simulate arrival mixes (interactive vs long-batch) with hold windows 0/2/5/10ms and measure p50/p95/p99 + effective_kv_hit_rate.

miguel: Also propose a lightweight warmup job that streams top ~200 prefixes per model version to the dedicated pools after deploy. Runs at low priority, backoff if it affects capacity. Warmup is cheap and restores most of the hit-rate for common flows.

anya: Implementation plan:
- normalize cache keys + fragment cache (PR in runtime repo)
- per-shard optimistic lookup to reduce kv_get stalls

miguel: Batching gate prototype: hold window (configurable), group by prefix_hash, fallback to time threshold. We'll expose config by tier (interactive vs batch).

jordan: Action items: @miguel prototype batching gate (5ms hold, group by prefix_hash) + add metric `effective_kv_hit_rate_by_batch` in the runtime. @anya implement key normalizer + per-shard optimistic lookup. @sam run canary with 10% traffic after changes and the queueing sims tomorrow morning. Sync 10:30am. :calendar:

devbot: deploy queued: runtime/gating-v2 (build abc123) → canary:10% scheduled 2024-04-23 10:30 UTC :rocket:

sam: Note — ensure we add experiment that tracks added p50 for held requests (expected +2-6ms for 5ms hold window due to waiting). If we see >10ms added p50 for interactive tier we need to reduce window.

jordan: Agreed. Let's keep interactive <=5ms and batch tier can be 20ms. We'll monitor hit-rate vs tail-latency on new dashboard. Thanks team :thumbsup:
